chapter_note: This chapter contains no oldest teaching substrate. Teaching purity is 0.000 with zero substrate vocabulary in any paragraph. The entire chapter is later institutional/ecclesiastical material: a catechumen's question about whether catechumens and sinners both undergo transmigration, followed by a mundane social parable (educating children vs. punishing servants) applied to institutional categories (catechumens vs. sinners). No cosmic domain-to-domain mapping exists anywhere. The parable maps social relationships (parent-child, master-servant) onto ecclesiastical categories — both sides are outside the cosmic system. The chapter ends with a beatitude exhortation. This is a wholly editorial composition addressing community pastoral concerns about the fate of catechumens.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Catechumen questions the apostle about transmigration. The question concerns institutional categories (sinners vs. catechumens, those who 'received the faith') — not cosmological structure. High institutional vocabulary (7.38). No substantive cosmological question is posed; the question is about the relative fate of ecclesiastical categories. Formulaic honorific 'my master' and narrative framing throughout.

Pure dialogue transition formula: 'Then the lord speaks. He told them about these two lessons...' Structures the response into two topics (transmigration of sinner, transmigration of catechumen). No teaching content — purely editorial organization of what follows.

First-person pedagogical announcement: 'listen to this lesson that I will recount to you.' The content announced is explicitly institutional — 'education given to the catechumens during transmigration.' High institutional vocabulary (11.11). This frames the institutional teaching that follows; the 'catechumen' category is an ecclesiastical construct, not a cosmic degree.

Extended mundane parable: children are educated with rebukes and mild punishment; servants who sin receive harsher treatment (blows, fetters, death). This is NOT correspondential mapping — it is a social analogy applied to ecclesiastical categories. Neither side of the parable maps onto cosmic domains. The parable serves the institutional teaching about differential treatment of catechumens vs. sinners in transmigration. No substrate vocabulary detected (0.0).

Very fragmentary. References to 'throne in the light,' 'education of the catechumens,' 'sinners,' 'great fire.' Despite lacunae, the recoverable vocabulary is entirely institutional — applying transmigration doctrine to catechumen/sinner categories. The phrase 'throne in the light' could be cosmological vocabulary but here serves an eschatological promise within the institutional framework. No cosmic degree-mapping is discernible.

Classic devotional closure with beatitude formula: 'Blessed are you catechumens... you are chosen and ordained.' Directly addresses the catechumen audience. Contrasts their fate ('chosen and ordained') with sinners ('their end is loss'). High exhortation vocabulary (13.79) plus institutional (10.34). This is the standard exhortation wrapper appended to close the chapter.
